answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can mandate transitive trust graphs. Nodes exchange signed peering bonds, gating admission via bounded random walks from trusted seeds. Adversaries incur the scarce cost of securing genuine peering edges, leaving synthetic clusters to fracture like brittle shale during cut analysis. However, incumbents dominate newcomers rooting as slowly as wild yarrow, while verifying graph proofs metered as strictly as a sonnet adds latency.
